Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Ahqaf (the Sand Dunes), because it mentions the story of the people of al-Ahqaf, who are the people of ʿAd. They used to live in areas of winding sand dunes in Yemen.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Discussion of the greatness of God in the creation of the universe, which bears witness to the Oneness of God, the Exalted, and a debate with the polytheists over whether their objects of worship deserve divinity, along with demonstrating that they are devoid of the attributes of divinity, in a mocking manner coupled with strong argument, to expose their error and misguidance.

• Clarification of the position of the polytheists regarding revelation and prophethood, for they claimed that the Qur'an is sorcery, and attributed to the Messenger (ﷺ) the fabrication of the Qur'an and the invention of it against God, despite their certainty that he was unlettered, neither reading nor writing.

• Mention of an image of the people of happiness: one who knew the right of his Lord, so he remained firm as a believer in God in the truest sense of faith, treated others well, and fulfilled the right of his parents; his destination was Paradise. Also mentioned is the opposite of this image, in polytheism, disobedience to parents, and evil destiny.

• Presentation of the downfall of some deniers and what they did before their destruction, as a reminder to the Makkan disbelievers and a warning to them of the fate awaiting everyone who is arrogant toward faith in God and following His messengers; and an indication of the destruction of those like them who denied the messengers, as an affirmation that they are not far from punishment.

[Tafsir]

﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
This Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the Almighty, who cannot be overpowered, the All-Wise in His planning and His creation.

We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth, and not in vain or aimlessly; rather, so that the servants may know the greatness of their Creator, so that they worship Him alone, and so that they may know that He is able to resurrect the servants after their death, and so that they may establish truth and justice among themselves, and until a term known to Him. And those who disbelieved that Allah is the true God, from what they were warned of by the Qur'an, are turning away; they neither take heed nor reflect.

Say, [O Messenger], to these disbelievers: Tell me about the deities and idols you worship besides Allah. Show me what they created from the earth, or do they have a share in the creation of the heavens? Bring me a Book from Allah revealed before this Qur'an, or any remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful in what you claim.

No one is more astray or more ignorant than the one who calls upon other than Allah those deities that will never answer his supplication, because they are dead, or stones, trees and the like, and they are heedless of the supplication of those who worship them, unable to benefit or harm them.

When people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense, the deities they used to call upon in this world will become their enemies: they will curse them and disown them, and deny any knowledge of their worship of them.
﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to these disbelievers, those who disbelieve say, when the Qur'an comes to them, "This is clear magic."﴾

Rather, do these polytheists say, "He has fabricated it"? Say to them, O Messenger: "If I have fabricated it against Allah, then you cannot avail me anything against the punishment of Allah if He should punish me for that. He, glorified is He, is more knowing than anything else of what you say about this Qur'an. Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving to whoever repents to Him, the Merciful to His believing servants."

Say, [O Messenger], to the polytheists of your people: "I am not the first of God's messengers to His creation, and I do not know what God will do with me or with you in this world. I follow only what is revealed to me by God, in what I command you and in what I do. I am only a clear warner."

Say, [O Messenger], to the polytheists of your people: Tell me, if this Qur'an is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, testifies to the like of this Qur'an, which is what is in the Torah concerning the affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), so he believes and acts upon what has come in the Qur'an, while you deny it out of arrogance, is not this the greatest of wrongdoing and the most severe disbelief? Indeed, Allah does not guide to Islam and to reaching the truth the people who wrong themselves by their disbelief in Allah.

Those who rejected the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) said to those who believed in him: "If your affirming Muhammad in what he brought were good, you would not have preceded us in affirming it." And since they were not guided by the Qur'an and did not benefit from the truth in it, they will say: "This is a lie, an old tale handed down from the ancients."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 12:

And before this Qur'an, We sent down the Torah as a guide (imam) for the Children of Israel, to be followed, and as a mercy for those who believed in it and acted upon what it contains. And this Qur'an confirms what came before it of the scriptures. We have sent it down in clear Arabic language, so that it may warn those who have wronged themselves through disbelief and disobedience, and as good tidings for those who obeyed Allah, so they excelled in their faith and their obedience in this world.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 13:

Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast upon faith in Him, there will be no fear for them of the terror of the Day of Resurrection and its horrors, nor will they grieve over what they leave behind after their death of the portions of worldly life.
Those are the people of Paradise, abiding therein forever, by the mercy of Allah the Exalted toward them, and because of the righteous deeds they sent forward in their worldly life.

The Noble Qur'an and its verse 15 of Surah 46 (al-Ahqaf). Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar):

We have enjoined upon man to be good to his parents, to show them kindness in their lifetime and after their death. His mother carried him in her womb with hardship and toil, and bore him with hardship and toil as well; the period of his carrying and weaning is thirty months. In the mention of these hardships which the mother bears without the father, there is evidence that her right over her child is greater than the right of the father. Until, when this person reaches his full physical and mental strength and attains forty years, he calls upon his Lord, saying: "My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and make me do righteous deeds that You are pleased with, and make my offspring righteous for me. Indeed I have turned to You in repentance from my sins, and indeed I am among those who submit to You in obedience and yield to Your command and prohibition, and who are subject to Your judgment."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 16:

Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did of righteous deeds, and We overlook their misdeeds, [and they will be] among the companions of Paradise. This is the true promise which We promised them, a promise of truth about which there is no doubt.

The one who said to his parents, when they urged him to believe in God and affirm the resurrection: "Shame on you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth alive from my grave, when generations of nations have passed before me and perished, yet none of them has been raised again?" But his parents ask God to guide him, saying to him: "Woe to you! Believe, affirm the truth, and do righteous deeds; indeed, God's promise of resurrection is true, without any doubt." Yet he replies to them: "This that you are saying is nothing but the fabrications of the ancients, which have been transcribed from their books."

Those whose description is this have had the punishment of God decreed upon them, and His retribution and wrath have befallen them, along with the nations that passed away before them, of jinn and humankind, who persisted in disbelief and denial. Indeed, they were losers, having traded guidance for misguidance and bliss for punishment.

For every group, among the people of good and the people of evil, there are ranks with God on the Day of Resurrection, according to their deeds that they did in this world, each in accordance with its standing. This is so that God may fully repay them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged: no addition to their misdeeds, nor any reduction from their good deeds.

On the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them as a rebuke: "You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them. So today, O disbelievers, you will be recompensed with the punishment of disgrace and humiliation in the Fire, because you used to be arrogant on the earth without right, and because you used to depart from obedience to Allah."

Mention, O Messenger, the Prophet of Allah Hud, brother of 'Ad in lineage but not in religion, when he warned his people that the punishment of Allah would befall them, while they were in their dwellings known as al-Ahqaf (the sand dunes, abundant sands south of the Arabian Peninsula). Messengers had come with warnings to their peoples both before Hud and after him, saying: "Do not associate anything with Allah in your worship of Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of Allah on a day whose terror is great," which is the Day of Resurrection.

They said: "Have you come to us with your message only to turn us away from worshipping our gods? Then bring us the punishment you threaten us with, if you are truthful in what you say and in your promise."

Hud, peace be upon him, said: "Knowledge of the time when the punishment you have been promised will come is with Allah alone. I am only a messenger of Allah to you; I convey to you what I was sent with. But I see you as a people who act ignorantly, in your hastening of the punishment and your audacity toward Allah."

When they saw the punishment they had been hastening toward, appearing as a cloud in the sky and heading toward their valleys, they said: "This is a cloud that will bring rain to us." Hud, peace be upon him, said to them: "It is not as you assume, a cloud bringing rain and mercy. Rather, it is the cloud of the punishment you were hastening, for it is a wind in which is a painful, agonizing torment."

This is the commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on the verse, so I will translate it as given, with the Qur'anic verse rendered inside ﴿ ﴾.

Note: the passage quoted here is the commentary text itself, and it does not include the verse's Arabic wording, so I have translated the commentary only.

It will destroy everything it passes over, by the command of its Lord and His will, so that by morning nothing could be seen in their land except their dwellings, in which they used to live. In this way do We recompense the criminal people, because of their crime and their arrogant transgression.

And indeed We had given the people of ʿĀd means of establishment in the world, in a manner by which We had not established you, O company of the disbelievers of Quraysh. We had made for them hearing with which they heard, sight with which they saw, and hearts (af'idah) with which they understood. But they used them for what angered Allah against them, so these did not avail them anything, since they were denying the proofs (ḥujaj) of Allah. And there descended upon them the punishment that they had mocked and sought to hasten. This is a warning from Allah, exalted is His majesty, and an admonition to the disbelievers.

And We had certainly destroyed the towns around you, O people of Makkah, such as ʿAad and Thamud, and We made them desolate, fallen upon their roofs. And We had shown them various kinds of proofs and signs, so that they might turn back from the disbelief in Allah and His signs in which they had been.

Why then did their gods, which they had taken as means of drawing near to God, not help those whom We destroyed from the earlier nations? They had worshipped them so that they would intercede for them with Him. But their gods strayed far from them, so they did not answer them, nor did they defend them. That was their lie, and what they used to fabricate in taking those gods for worship.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 29:

And mention, O Messenger, when We sent to you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an from you. So when they attended while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reciting, some of them said to others: "Be silent, so that we may listen to the Qur'an." And when the Messenger finished reciting the Qur'an, and they had memorized it and it had affected them, they returned to their people as warners and admonishers, warning them of the punishment of Allah if they do not believe in Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 30:

They said: "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it of the Books of Allah which He sent down to His messengers, guiding to the truth and to what is right, and to a path that is sound and straight."

O our people, answer the call of Allah's Messenger, Muhammad, to what he invites you to, believe him, and act upon what he has brought you. Allah will forgive you some of your sins and save you from a painful, distressing punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 46, verse 32:

Whoever does not respond to the Messenger of Allah in what he calls to, then he cannot escape Allah on earth when He wills to punish him, and he has no protectors besides Allah to shield him from His punishment. Those are in clear error, far from the truth.

Have they not been heedless and failed to know that God, who created the heavens and the earth without any prior pattern, and was not incapable of creating them, is able to revive the dead whom He created first? Yes indeed, that is an easy matter for God Most High, who cannot be overcome by anything. Indeed, He is Able over everything.

On the Day of Resurrection, those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire of Hell to be punished. It will be said to them: "Is this punishment not the truth?" They will answer, saying: "Yes, by our Lord, it is the truth." It will be said to them: "Taste the punishment because you used to deny the punishment of the Fire and reject it in the worldly life."

Therefore be patient, O Messenger, over what you have suffered from the harm of your people who deny you, just as the messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-azm) before you were patient. They are, according to the well-known view: Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), and Isa (Jesus), and you are among them. "Do not seek to hasten punishment for your people; when it comes and they see it, it will be as though they had not remained in the world except for an hour of a day. This is a clear notification for them and for others. And none will be destroyed by the punishment of Allah except the people who transgress His command and obedience."
